Survivor 51 is the fifty-first season of the CBS competitive reality television series Survivor.

Production[]

During the In the Hands of the Fans live reunion, host Jeff Probst explained that the season would heavily incorporate past game mechanics, Hidden Immunity Idols, and other advantages to keep castaways on their toes. He branded the season as the beginning of the "Open Era" of Survivor. Probst teased:

“ The "Open Era" is that anything “that has ever happened at any time on the show can happen in any season at any time in any order without any warning.[3] ”

—Jeff Probst


While the show will continue identifying seasons by number, Probst stated that the producers would reconsider using themed seasons again in the future.[4]

Twists/Changes[]

  • 26-Day Game
  • Tribe Division: The castaways were divided into 2 tribes. No unifying theme was used in dividing the tribes.
  • The Open Era: The new overarching theme for the series as a whole, where any twist Survivor has ever done in a previous season (game mechanics, idols, advantages, etc.) has the potential to show up at any given moment.
  • Exile Island
  • Shot in the Dark
  • Hidden Immunity Idol: Hidden immunity idols would be hidden at both tribe camps. In addition, there is an idol at Exile Island on Day 2, but can only be claimed if the person sent there can complete a challenge in the allotted time.
  • Million-Dollar Coin Toss: At some point during the season, someone will step up to flip a coin, calling either "heads" or "tails". If it lands on what the castaway calls, they will add a million dollars to the prize money. However if their call is wrong, they will be eliminated, and the million dollars is banked until the following season. Every season where the coin toss fails, an extra million dollars will be at stake for the following season. Once the coin toss is finally successful, the cycle will restart for the following season.
  • Mutiny: On Day 6, each tribe sent a member to the rival tribe's camp. These castaways could speak to the other tribe, and had the choice to either return to their original tribe or stay at their new tribe.
    • Extra Vote

Trivia[]

  • Survivor 51 is the first season since Winners at War to start with only two competing tribes.[5]
  • Survivor 51 is the first season since Fiji to start with an odd number of castaways, with 21 castaways competing.
    • This is the first season to intentionally do so, as Fiji was intended to have 20 castaways prior to Mellisa McNulty withdrawing.
  • Survivor 51 is the third season to start with an unequal number of male and female castaways, after Fiji and San Juan del Sur.
    • This is the first season to intentionally do so as well, as Fiji was intended to have 20 castaways, and San Juan del Sur also intended to have 20 castaways prior to Doo Kim withdrawing, causing So Kim to have to withdraw as well.
    • This season also marks the first season with more female castaways (11) than male castaways (10).
